title: Indian Independence Day 2026: Major Events Across the US This August
excerpt: From the iconic NYC India Day Parade to celebrations in Atlanta, Boston, and the Bay Area, Indian Americans are gearing up to mark India's 80th Independence Day with parades, festivals, and cultural showcases spanning the country.
body:
Indian Americans across the United States are preparing for a packed calendar of Independence Day events this August, as communities from coast to coast organize parades, cultural festivals, and flag-hoisting ceremonies to mark India's 80th Independence Day on August 15.

With nearly five million people of Indian origin living in the US, the celebrations have grown into some of the country's most prominent multicultural events, drawing thousands of attendees, elected officials, and this year, Bollywood celebrities.

New York Leads the Way

The Federation of Indian Associations' India Day Parade in Manhattan remains the marquee event on the calendar. Scheduled for August 16, the parade will follow the annual hoisting of the Indian tricolor at Times Square on August 15. The procession down Madison Avenue celebrates the diversity of Indian culture through performances by community groups of all ages and has grown steadily each year.

On Long Island, the 15th India Day Parade USA will take place on August 23 in Hicksville, New York. A curtain-raiser event held in June at the Theodore Roosevelt Executive & Legislative Building in Mineola drew more than 250 attendees, including New York State Senator Steven D. Rhoads and Consul Tsewang Gyaltson from the Consulate General of India.

"The India Day Parade has become a symbol of pride and identity for Indian Americans."

— Deepak Bansal, President, India Day Parade USA

Major Celebrations Coast to Coast

In the Bay Area, two major events anchor the West Coast celebrations. The Federation of Indo Americans' FOG India Day Parade in Fremont, California runs August 15-16, with the main parade stepping off on August 16 at 11 AM. Bollywood actors Sanya Malhotra and Abhimanyu Dassani are this year's Grand Marshals. The event also features a mela with food, shopping, book, and craft booths. Tickets cost $5 to $6.

Also in the Bay Area, the Association of Indo Americans is hosting "Swades," a night market and celebration at Plaza de Cesar Chavez in downtown San Jose on August 15. The event runs from 2 PM to 10:30 PM and includes an attempt at a record-breaking Indian human flag formation.

Atlanta's Indian American Cultural Association is marking three decades of its Festival of India on August 15 at the Gas South Convention Center in Duluth, Georgia. The celebration holds special significance this year: India's 80th Independence Day coincides with America's 250th anniversary. The ticketed event features music, food, yoga, chess, dance, and cultural displays from 8 AM to 5 PM.

Boston, Michigan, and the Midwest

The Indian Association of Greater Boston is hosting its India Day Festival, titled "Colors of India," on August 15 at the DCR Hatch Memorial Shell overlooking the Charles River. The event showcases performances and cultural displays celebrating India's diversity against one of Boston's most scenic outdoor venues.

In Michigan, the India League of America is hosting India Day on August 15 at Vibe Credit Union Showplace in Novi, about 25 miles from Detroit. Former Indian cricket star Harbhajan Singh is this year's celebrity guest, adding a sports dimension to the festivities that include traditional food, dance, and musical performances.

Southern Events from Charlotte to Florida

North Carolina's Hindu Center of Charlotte is organizing its Independence Day celebration under the theme "Maa Tujhe Pranaam" (Mother, I Salute You). The free, family-friendly event on August 15 features patriotic and folk performances, though registration is required on a first-come, first-served basis.

In Southern California, the India Association of Los Angeles is hosting its annual Independence Day celebration on August 22 at the Hjelte Sports Center in Encino. Dr. K.J. Srinivasa, the Consul General of India in Los Angeles, and Congressman Brad Sherman are the guests of honor. The event has been a fixture of the SoCal Indian community since 1999.

Florida's Association of Indians in America chapter hosts its celebration on August 18 at the Broward Center in Fort Lauderdale, with cultural programs, Indian food, and patriotic music.

A Growing Tradition

The scale of this year's events reflects the growing size and visibility of the Indian American community. Texas celebrations include events in Round Rock near Austin on August 15. In Virginia, the Anna Sudha Community Kitchens nonprofit is organizing a festival on August 17 at Dulles Town Center in Loudoun County, featuring Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam dance performances.

Most events are open to all, with some requiring advance registration or modest ticket purchases. For diaspora families looking to connect with their heritage, the August calendar offers no shortage of opportunities to celebrate India's independence thousands of miles from home.
